questions.stem: A Baltimore first applicant completes a course but has not passed its examination. What remains required before appointment?
questions.explanation: Initial Maryland applicants must complete the course and pass the examination.
feedback: Correct. Both requirements apply initially.
A seal does not replace the exam.
Vendor selection is a different requirement.
Education precedes appointment.

questions.stem: A renewing Maryland notary sees one FAQ eligibility paragraph saying renewals need an exam. Which requirement is supported by §18-102 and the dedicated renewal instructions?
options: Every renewal must retake the initial exam
questions.explanation: The statute and dedicated renewal page require the renewal course, while the broad FAQ paragraph conflicts.
feedback: The course remains required.
Correct. Preserve the documented first/renewal distinction.
The controlling statute specifies course completion for renewal.
Handbook purchase does not itself certify course completion.

questions.stem: A provider offers a Maryland final of ten questions. What minimum does COMAR require?
questions.explanation: COMAR 01.02.08.16 F requires at least 20 multiple-choice questions.
feedback: Five falls below the minimum.
Ten falls below the minimum.
Correct. Twenty is a minimum, not a universal exact count.
Fifty is the bank minimum, not an exact final count.

questions.stem: A candidate scores 79% on the required final. What result is needed for the Certificate of Passing?
questions.explanation: The provider issues a passing certificate for a score of at least 80%.
feedback: Attendance alone is not a pass.
Fifty percent is too low.
A surety cannot waive the standard.
Correct. The regulatory threshold is 80%.

questions.stem: A final examination question has two answers and both may be correct. What format does COMAR require?
options: Four choices with only one correct answer
questions.explanation: Each question has four multiple-choice answers with one correct answer.
feedback: Correct. The specified item format is explicit.
Multiple correct options do not meet this rule.
The regulation specifies multiple choice.
Two choices do not satisfy the four-answer requirement.

questions.stem: A course provider keeps a bank of 30 questions for repeated Maryland examinations. What minimum bank applies?
questions.explanation: The provider needs a robust bank of at least 50 different questions.
feedback: Ten is below the minimum.
Correct. The bank minimum is 50.
Twenty is the administered-exam minimum.
The regulation expressly requires a bank.

questions.stem: An applicant finishes the course but fails the final. What must the provider offer a qualified retester?
questions.explanation: A course completer who scores below 80% is qualified for an opportunity to retest.
feedback: Failure does not create a commission.
An interview does not replace the required result.
Correct. COMAR requires a retest opportunity.
No permanent exemption is created.

questions.stem: An electronic examination ends and the provider says results will be withheld indefinitely. What does COMAR require?
options: A mailed result in seven years
Immediate passing/failure scoring at the session's conclusion
questions.explanation: The testing system must provide immediate scoring at the end of the session.
feedback: Seven years does not meet immediacy.
The examination must be scored.
An estimate does not meet the scoring requirement.
Correct. The applicant receives the result immediately.

questions.stem: A first applicant receives only a course-completion certificate and asks whether the application evidence is complete. What second certificate is required?
questions.explanation: The new-applicant page requires both completion and passing certificates.
feedback: Correct. Upload both required certificates.
A marriage license is unrelated.
Insurance does not certify examination passing.
An invoice does not establish passing.

questions.stem: An applicant uses a course unrelated to Maryland law and outside the authorized list. What should be verified?
options: Maryland provider authorization and course coverage
Only whether it included a stamp
questions.explanation: Use an authorized Maryland course and examination provider.
feedback: Price does not establish authorization.
Correct. Verify the official provider list and coverage.
Popularity does not establish approval.
A stamp bundle does not certify the course.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old has the required education and asks to apply. What statutory qualification is missing?
questions.explanation: Maryland requires applicants to be at least 18.
feedback: Office ownership is not the age requirement.
A law license is not required ordinarily.
Correct. Education does not waive minimum age.
Bank employment is not required.

questions.stem: A Virginia resident works regularly in Maryland and wants a Maryland commission. What additional statutory condition concerns the home state?
options: The home state must share a county name
The home state must issue identical seals
The employer must own a courthouse
The home state must allow working Maryland residents to serve as its notaries
questions.explanation: Nonresident eligibility includes the statutory reciprocity condition.
feedback: County names do not establish reciprocity.
Seal design does not establish reciprocal eligibility.
Employer property is irrelevant.
Correct. Verify the home-state reciprocal opportunity.

questions.stem: A Maryland resident works in a different county and wants to substitute the office address for the home address on the application. What do official instructions require?
options: The actual home address with the required address evidence
questions.explanation: The application requires the resident's home address and its verification.
feedback: Correct. Employment address does not replace residence.
A borrowed address does not establish residence.
The work address is additional information.
Proximity does not establish the lawful residence record.
questions.reference: Work address and home address FAQ

questions.stem: The applicant's ID address differs from the application address. Which additional record does the FAQ require?
options: The matching MVA Change of Address Card
questions.explanation: The FAQ identifies the MVA Change of Address Card for the mismatch.
feedback: The FAQ specifies the government address evidence.
Correct. Supply the required matching card.
A profile does not provide the stated evidence.
A seal order does not verify the home address.

questions.stem: A first application is prepared without any reference contact details. How many references does the FAQ list?
questions.explanation: The new-applicant checklist lists contact information for three references.
feedback: One does not meet the checklist.
Two does not meet it.
Correct. Provide three reference contacts.
Ten is not the stated checklist count.

questions.stem: A resident chooses a state senator solely because the office is close to work. Which district matters for resident appointment?
options: Any senator selected by the stamp vendor
The senatorial district of residence, subject to lawful delegated approval
questions.explanation: Resident appointment follows the statutory district of residence and approval provisions.
feedback: Employment location does not replace residence.
A vendor cannot select the appointing district.
Recipient location is unrelated.
Correct. Use the residential legislative district.

questions.stem: The online application asks for the current state application fee. What amount do the new instructions state since January 22, 2024?
questions.explanation: The dedicated new-applicant page states a $25 application fee.
feedback: Correct. The fee changed to $25.
The page identifies $9 as an older amount.
The old service charge is not the current application fee.
$250 is not the stated fee.

questions.stem: An applicant pays online and assumes this immediately authorizes notarizing. What remaining event matters?
options: Approval followed by required court qualification and commission delivery
questions.explanation: Approval is followed by qualifying before the appropriate circuit-court clerk and receiving the commission.
feedback: An announcement does not qualify the applicant.
Correct. Payment is an application step.
A receipt does not supply qualification.
A journal purchase does not confer authority.

questions.stem: A newly approved applicant receives the state email directing a court appearance. What deadline applies?
options: Qualify within 30 days after the notice of appointment
questions.explanation: Section 18-103 requires qualification within 30 days after notice of appointment or renewal.
feedback: One year exceeds the statutory period.
Seven is not the stated qualification period.
Correct. Track the 30-day qualification deadline.
First appointment also requires qualification.

questions.stem: A current notary renews successfully and assumes the old oath covers the next term. What do the official instructions require?
options: Only an email to the employer
Take the oath again when issued the new commission
questions.explanation: The FAQ requires the court oath whenever a new commission is issued.
feedback: Renewal includes a new oath.
The receipt does not administer an oath.
Employer notice does not qualify the new term.
Correct. Repeat the court qualification.

questions.stem: A Maryland notary thinks the commission is valid for life. What is the statutory term?
questions.explanation: Section 18-103(c) establishes a four-year commission term.
feedback: Correct. The term is four years.
One year is not the ordinary statutory term.
Seven years is another state's rule.
The commission is not lifetime authority.

questions.stem: A notary's expiration is fifty days away. What ordinary renewal window applies?
options: At any time in the four-year term
questions.explanation: The official FAQ states the renewal period begins 60 days before expiration.
feedback: The window begins before expiration.
Correct. Fifty days is within the stated window.
Ten days is narrower than the stated window.
The routine renewal window is not the entire term.

questions.stem: A notary's commission expired 45 days ago. What route do official instructions identify after the 30-day post-expiration renewal period?
questions.explanation: Beyond 30 days after expiration, the FAQ directs a new commission application.
feedback: Expired authority cannot be assumed.
Supplies do not renew authority.
Correct. Use the new-application route.
No automatic lifetime extension exists.

questions.stem: A commissioned Pennsylvania notary moves to Maryland and wants to transfer the commission. What does the FAQ say?
options: Only a stamp exchange is needed
A Maryland application is required because commissions are not transferable
questions.explanation: The official FAQ says out-of-state commissions do not transfer to Maryland.
feedback: The FAQ expressly rejects automatic transfer.
Changing supplies does not create Maryland authority.
An employer cannot transfer public office.
Correct. Apply under Maryland's requirements.

questions.stem: An applicant wants the commission in a nickname absent from government photo ID. What official naming rule applies?
options: Use a permitted name matching the government ID without the nickname
Let the employer choose a title
questions.explanation: The FAQ requires the commissioned name to match the government photo ID and excludes nicknames.
feedback: Correct. Follow the official naming guidance.
A handle does not establish the required commissioned name.
An employer title does not replace the person's identity.
A notary commission identifies the individual.

questions.stem: A notary adds Ph.D. to the proposed commissioned name. What do official instructions say?
options: Do not add such a title to the commissioned name
questions.explanation: The FAQ excludes added titles such as Ph.D. or Esq. from the commissioned name.
feedback: The official guidance says the opposite.
Correct. Use the permitted name matching ID.
Customer preference does not set commission naming.
A title cannot replace the surname.

questions.stem: A notary changes a personal email address but does not update the state for months. What COMAR period applies?
options: Notify the Secretary within thirty days
questions.explanation: COMAR.09 requires notice within 30 days for the listed information changes.
feedback: One year exceeds the period.
Renewal can be too late.
Correct. Report the email change within 30 days.
The regulation requires reporting.

questions.stem: A notary relies only on an employer email account that becomes inactive on departure. What responsibility does COMAR assign?
options: Only the employer updates the state
Maintain a current active personal email with the Secretary
questions.explanation: COMAR.10 places responsibility on the notary for a current active personal email.
feedback: The rule expressly assigns responsibility.
The notary remains responsible.
The rule uses email except for enforcement correspondence.
Correct. Keep the personal contact active.

questions.stem: A Maryland resident moves to another county during the term and updates the address. What does the FAQ say about a new oath solely for that address change?
options: No new oath is required solely for the address change
A new oath is always required within 24 hours
The commission immediately becomes a marriage license
The address must never be updated
questions.explanation: The FAQ says an address change does not require appearing for another oath.
feedback: Correct. The update obligation still applies.
The FAQ does not require this new oath.
A move does not change the office type.
The state record must be updated.

questions.stem: A notary chooses the FAQ option to obtain a commission under a new legal name during the term. What happens to expiration?
options: It automatically resets for four full years
It keeps the current commission's expiration date
questions.explanation: The name-change commission expires on the existing commission's date.
feedback: The FAQ expressly says no new four-year term.
Correct. The current expiration date remains.
The change does not create lifetime authority.
An employer cannot set the term.

questions.stem: A provider offers a virtual Maryland course and asks whether asynchronous delivery is categorically forbidden. What does COMAR permit?
options: Virtual delivery including synchronous or asynchronous online study
questions.explanation: COMAR.15 C permits virtual or in-person courses and defines virtual to include both online forms.
feedback: The regulation expressly permits virtual courses.
It is not limited to live television.
Correct. Approved virtual formats may include either form.
Authorized provider courses are expressly contemplated.

questions.stem: A provider's practice questions never cover ethics or the handbook. What does COMAR require of course coverage?
options: Maryland laws, regulations, ethics, procedures and the handbook topics
questions.explanation: COMAR.16 A requires full coverage of the specified subjects.
feedback: Coverage is broader than stamp design.
Real-estate pricing is not the stated course scope.
Marketing does not provide the required education.
Correct. All prescribed notarial subjects must be covered.

questions.stem: A candidate assumes the minimum twenty-question rule establishes an exact statewide count and clock. What is accurate?
options: It is a minimum count and no uniform time limit was verified
Every examination is exactly twenty questions and two minutes
Every provider must use fifty administered questions
questions.explanation: The rule says at least 20. The opened provisions do not establish a uniform exam time limit.
feedback: Correct. Preserve the distinction between minimum and exact specifications.
That exact count and duration are unsupported.
Fifty is the bank minimum.
The regulation establishes several standards.

questions.stem: A notary will be traveling throughout the ordinary renewal window. What does the FAQ recommend?
options: Contact the office before leaving for early-renewal instructions
Let a coworker renew under their name
questions.explanation: The FAQ directs advance contact for instructions when travel prevents ordinary-window renewal.
feedback: Ignoring expiration does not preserve authority.
Correct. The office provides the stated exceptional procedure.
Another person cannot substitute their identity.
A seal does not extend the term.

questions.stem: A notary fails to qualify and pay the required court fees within the statutory deadline. What does §18-103 provide?
options: Only a warning with no effect
Revocation, with possible reinstatement for good cause by the Secretary
questions.explanation: The statute provides revocation for failure to qualify and permits good-cause reinstatement.
feedback: The failure does not confer practice authority.
The statute specifies revocation.
Correct. Apply the actual qualification consequence and remedy.
No automatic transfer results.

questions.stem: A notary recognizes a customer's name from advertisements but has never dealt with the customer. What supports statutory personal knowledge?
options: Dealings sufficient to provide reasonable certainty of identity
questions.explanation: Personal knowledge requires sufficient dealings with the individual.
feedback: Fame alone is not the stated standard.
A surname match does not establish knowledge.
Correct. The statutory dealings standard applies.
Payment does not establish identity.

questions.stem: An unknown signer presents a qualifying consular identification document. Is that category expressly listed in Maryland's identity statute?
questions.explanation: Section 18-206(b)(1)(i) expressly includes consular identification.
feedback: The statute lists several document categories.
Employer approval does not define the statute.
The category is not limited to real estate.
Correct. Assess the credential under the applicable identity requirements.

questions.stem: A signer offers another type of government ID with a photograph but no signature. What does the alternative category require?
options: Both signature and photograph, satisfactory to the officer
Only a photograph in all cases
questions.explanation: The alternative government-ID category requires both signature and photograph.
feedback: Correct. Maryland's alternative category uses both features.
A photograph alone omits the stated signature requirement.
A phone number does not supply the required elements.
An address does not supply the missing signature.

questions.stem: A witness unknown personally to the officer appears, is identified by qualifying consular ID and verifies the principal's identity on affirmation. Which route may apply?
questions.explanation: A credible witness may be known or identified through the listed credentials, including consular ID.
feedback: The statute includes credential identification.
Correct. Apply the appearance and sworn-verification requirements.
An employer guarantee is a different proposal.
The method is not limited to a personal friend.

questions.stem: A witness offers an unsworn text naming a signer. What element does the statutory witness method require?
options: Verification on oath or affirmation by the appearing credible witness
questions.explanation: The witness method requires personal appearance and verification on oath or affirmation.
feedback: A credit report is not the required witness declaration.
A contract is not the witness's sworn verification.
Correct. An unsworn message alone is insufficient.
An invoice does not establish identity.

questions.stem: A credential leaves the officer uncertain about the appearing person's identity. What may the officer require?
options: Additional information or identity credentials necessary for assurance
questions.explanation: Section 18-206(c) permits additional identity assurance.
feedback: A return promise does not establish current identity.
A fee cannot cure uncertainty.
Manager approval does not replace the officer's determination.
Correct. Request additional lawful identity evidence.

questions.stem: A courier brings a customer's signed record and driver's-license copy while the customer is absent. What remains required?
options: Only a second copy of the ID
questions.explanation: The statement-maker or signer must appear, including through a compliant remote procedure where used.
feedback: Correct. A courier cannot supply the customer's appearance.
A different signature does not perform the customer's act.
An employer cannot waive appearance.
More copies do not create appearance.

questions.stem: A signer appears through lawful communication technology. Does §18-205 categorically require physical presence for every act?
options: Yes, remote appearance is never allowed
Yes, unless the signer owns land
Yes, unless the signer is an attorney
questions.explanation: The statute permits a remotely located individual to satisfy appearance by communication technology under the lawful procedure.
feedback: Subsection(b) expressly recognizes remote appearance.
Correct. The full remote requirements still apply.
Land ownership does not determine appearance.
Attorney status is not the remote-appearance exception.

questions.stem: An individual physically unable to sign directs a caregiver to sign the person's name. Who must appear concurrently?
options: Neither if a phone call is made
questions.explanation: Section 18-208 requires the principal and directed signer to appear concurrently.
feedback: The principal's appearance is still required.
Employer presence does not replace either participant.
Correct. The statutory participants appear together.
A call does not remove concurrent appearance.

questions.stem: A disabled principal asks the notarial officer to be the person affixing the principal's signature. What does §18-208 allow?
options: The officer automatically signs both roles
Any absent person may choose the helper
A directed individual other than the notarial officer
questions.explanation: The statute excludes the notarial officer as the directed third-person signer.
feedback: The statute specifies a different individual.
The principal directs the signer.
The employer is not the sole permitted person.
Correct. Use the stated directed-signature procedure.

questions.stem: A directed signature is completed under §18-208. What notation is required?
options: Words identifying who affixed the signature and at whose direction
A statement that the notary signed for the principal
questions.explanation: The record carries the prescribed or similar directed-signature statement.
feedback: Correct. The statement identifies both participants' roles.
A receipt does not describe the execution.
A job title omits the principal's direction.
The officer is not the permitted directed signer.

questions.stem: A helper arrives alone with written authority from a physically unable principal. Does that satisfy §18-208's appearance method?
options: Yes, every written instruction replaces presence
No, the principal must also appear concurrently
Yes, if the helper is a nurse
Yes, if the fee is waived
questions.explanation: The statute requires concurrent appearance of the principal and directed signer.
feedback: The required concurrent appearance remains.
Correct. The absent principal leaves the method incomplete.
Occupation does not waive the requirement.
Free service still requires the lawful procedure.

questions.stem: A signer appears confused about the transaction and cannot demonstrate understanding. What permits refusal under §18-207?
options: Being unsatisfied that the individual is competent or has capacity
questions.explanation: Subject to other law, the officer may refuse on the stated competence/capacity basis.
feedback: The statutory issue is capacity.
Length alone is not that finding.
Correct. Evaluate the individual's capacity.
Age alone does not answer the required judgment.

questions.stem: A companion pressures an unwilling signer in the notary's presence. Which statutory issue matters?
options: Only how fast the appointment ends
Whether the signature is knowingly and voluntarily made
questions.explanation: The officer may refuse if not satisfied of knowing and voluntary signing.
feedback: Occupation does not resolve coercion.
Haste does not establish voluntariness.
Address does not resolve free choice.
Correct. The statutory voluntariness assessment applies.

questions.stem: A trustee acknowledges a record on behalf of a trust. What declaration accompanies representative execution?
options: Proper authority and signing as the represented entity's act
That the notary guarantees all trust assets
That no identity evidence is needed
questions.explanation: Representative acknowledgment includes proper authority and the represented person's or entity's act.
feedback: Correct. The statutory definition addresses these facts.
The notary does not guarantee assets.
The representative must still be identified.
The act does not appoint the notary as trustee.

questions.stem: An individual declares under affirmation that statements in a record are true. Which defined act fits?
questions.explanation: Verification is a solemn declaration of the statement's truth under oath or affirmation.
feedback: Copying is a different act.
Correct. This is the defined verification.
Renewal concerns public appointment.
Replacing a seal does not perform the truth declaration.

questions.stem: A person prefers affirmation rather than an oath. What does the Maryland verification definition allow?
options: Only an acknowledgment of the signature
questions.explanation: The statutory verification definition expressly permits either solemn form.
feedback: Affirmation is expressly included.
Acknowledgment does not automatically supply the requested truth declaration.
Correct. Administer the appropriate solemn form.
Verification requires the actual declaration.

questions.stem: A corporate agent signs an instrument and asks which short form reflects that capacity. What does §18-216 provide?
options: A representative acknowledgment identifying authority and represented party
questions.explanation: The representative acknowledgment form identifies the role and party represented.
feedback: An anonymous stamp does not record the act.
Copy certification is a different act.
A tax declaration does not record representative execution.
Correct. Use a sufficient accurate representative form.

questions.stem: A signature is to be witnessed. What does §18-204(c) require the officer to determine?
options: The appearing signer has the identity claimed while signing the record
The signer will repay every debt
The document has no legal risks
questions.explanation: The officer identifies the appearing individual signing the record.
feedback: Correct. The determination concerns the appearing signer.
Witnessing does not guarantee debt payment.
The act does not provide a legal-risk guarantee.
Ownership is not created by the act.

questions.stem: An acknowledgment customer is identified, but the officer is uncertain whose signature appears on the record. What determination remains?
options: That the record's signature is the individual's signature
That the document will be recorded
questions.explanation: Acknowledgment requires determining both the appearing person's identity and the person's signature on the record.
feedback: Employment does not settle the signature determination.
Correct. Identity and signature connection both matter.
Manufacturer is unrelated.
Future recording does not identify the signature.

questions.stem: A notary certifies a copy missing one page from the original. Which requirement fails?
options: The full, true and accurate reproduction determination
questions.explanation: Copy certification requires a full, true and accurate transcription or reproduction.
feedback: Handwriting is not the missing content issue.
Envelope size does not cure the omitted page.
Correct. The incomplete copy cannot support that statement.
Parking information is unrelated.

questions.stem: A printout of an electronic record is proposed for accurate-copy certification. Which act must the officer personally perform or supervise?
options: Printing the electronic record onto tangible medium
questions.explanation: Section 18-204(e) requires personally printing or supervising the printing.
feedback: Payment does not satisfy the printing requirement.
A greeting does not produce the certified record.
Advertising is unrelated.
Correct. The officer controls the stated print process.

questions.stem: An officer detects an error in the electronic signature on a record presented for tangible-copy certification. What applies?
options: Ignore the error if the title matches
Ask the customer to waive it
Use a bigger seal to cover it
questions.explanation: The statute prohibits this certification when a change or error in signature or other information is detected.
feedback: Correct. The detected error prevents the certification.
A matching title does not cure the error.
A waiver does not remove the statutory condition.
A seal cannot conceal the defect lawfully.

questions.stem: Before certifying an accurate tangible copy of an electronic record, what format determination must the officer reasonably make?
options: Only that the file opens on a phone
Whether the electronic record is in a tamper-evident format
Only that the filename is short
Only that the printer uses color
questions.explanation: Section 18-204(e) requires a reasonable tamper-evident-format determination.
feedback: Opening does not establish tamper evidence.
Correct. The integrity-format determination is required.
Filename length is unrelated.
Color printing does not establish electronic integrity.

questions.stem: A completed certificate omits the actual notarial jurisdiction. What must be added?
options: The jurisdiction in which the act is performed
questions.explanation: The certificate identifies the actual act's jurisdiction.
feedback: Preference does not determine venue.
Drafting location does not necessarily locate the act.
Correct. Use the actual jurisdiction.
Birthplace does not locate the ceremony.

questions.stem: A notary signs certificates in a manner unrelated to the signature filed with the circuit-court clerk. What does §18-215 require?
options: Signing in the same manner as on file with the appropriate clerk
questions.explanation: The certificate signature must follow the filed manner.
feedback: The customer cannot choose the official signature.
An employer name does not execute the individual's certificate.
The filed manner controls.
Correct. Use the signature manner on file.

questions.stem: A customer asks for the notary's certificate signature before the appearance and ceremony. What sequence is required?
options: Perform the act before signing or logically associating the certificate
Sign first if the fee is prepaid
Sign first if the employer promises completion
Let the customer supply facts later
questions.explanation: The officer cannot sign or associate the certificate until the act has been performed.
feedback: Correct. Certificate execution follows the actual act.
Prepayment does not authorize advance certification.
An employer promise does not perform the act.
Later facts cannot justify a pre-signed certificate.

questions.stem: A separate certificate is prepared for a paper instrument. What must connect them?
options: The certificate must be part of or securely attached to the record
questions.explanation: The tangible-record certificate must be part of or securely attached to that record.
feedback: Payment does not remove attachment.
Correct. Preserve the record-certificate association.
A description does not attach the certificate.
An invoice is a different record.

questions.stem: An electronic certificate is kept in a file unrelated to the electronic record it concerns. What is required?
options: Affixing or logically associating the certificate with the electronic record
questions.explanation: Section 18-215 requires proper association with the electronic record.
feedback: Wallpaper does not associate legal records.
A phone number does not connect the certificate.
Correct. The certificate belongs with the electronic record.
A receipt does not establish the required association.

questions.stem: A paper act is performed by a Maryland notary public, and the certificate has no official stamp. What does §18-215(b)(1) require?
options: Affix or emboss the official stamp on the certificate
questions.explanation: A notary public performing a tangible-record act must stamp or emboss the certificate.
feedback: The statute requires the official stamp.
The customer's signature does not supply the official stamp.
A watermark does not necessarily supply the required stamp.
Correct. Complete the mandatory tangible-record stamp.

questions.stem: A transaction certificate says only that the officer holds a commission, without describing any performed act. What must a sufficient certificate do?
options: Meet required fields and use a permitted form or sufficient actual-act description
questions.explanation: Section 18-215(c) allows sufficient forms or descriptions of the actual notarial actions.
feedback: Correct. The certificate must evidence the act.
Employer information does not describe the notarial event.
A course score does not certify this transaction.
A fee amount alone is insufficient.

questions.stem: A verified statement is to be notarized but no oath or affirmation is administered. What would the statutory definition still require?
options: The individual's actual oath or affirmation declaration
questions.explanation: Verification on oath or affirmation requires the solemn declaration itself.
feedback: Printed wording does not perform the declaration.
Correct. Administer the required oath or affirmation.
Payment does not administer the ceremony.
Employer approval does not perform the act.

questions.stem: An agent acting under a power of attorney appears and acknowledges execution for the principal. Is that a listed representative capacity?
options: Only if the notary prepared the power
Yes, agent or attorney-in-fact is expressly included
Only if no identity check occurs
questions.explanation: The representative-capacity definition includes an agent or attorney-in-fact for a principal.
feedback: The definition includes several capacities.
Preparation by the notary is not required.
Correct. The category is expressly listed.
The appearing agent still must be identified.

questions.stem: A notary verifies a statement by an identified individual but cannot connect the signature to that individual. What must the officer determine?
options: Only whether the customer has cash
Only whether the document is bound
That the signature on the statement is the individual's signature
questions.explanation: Section 18-204(b) requires the signature connection as well as identity.
feedback: Cash does not establish the signature.
Binding does not identify the signer.
Business hours are unrelated.
Correct. Both required determinations must be made.

questions.stem: The record has no certificate. What does the Maryland FAQ require the officer to do?
options: Affix a certificate by securely attaching it to the record
Ask the signer to accept no certificate
Keep an unattached generic certificate in a drawer
questions.explanation: The FAQ requires a securely attached certificate where one is absent.
feedback: Correct. Every act must be evidenced by a certificate.
A stamp alone does not supply the required certificate.
The signer cannot remove the statutory duty.
An unrelated loose form does not evidence the act.

questions.stem: A bank notary records only paid acts and omits free acknowledgments. What does Maryland require?
options: A journal chronicling all notarial acts
questions.explanation: Each notary must chronicle all acts in a journal.
feedback: Fees do not define journal scope.
The duty is broader than real estate.
Correct. Free acts remain within the journal duty.
In-person acts are also included.

questions.stem: A notary assumes a long-known neighbor's act needs no entry. What applies?
options: Personal knowledge removes all record duties
Journal the act and state personal knowledge as the identity basis
questions.explanation: The journal covers all acts and records personal knowledge when used.
feedback: Personal knowledge changes the recorded identity basis.
Client preference does not remove the duty.
The stamp does not replace the journal.
Correct. Record the act and actual basis.

questions.stem: An office journals Tuesday's notarizations only at month's end. What timing is required?
questions.explanation: Each journal entry is made contemporaneously with the act.
feedback: Correct. Enter the act when performed.
Annual summaries are too late.
A dispute does not trigger the original duty.
Renewal does not set entry timing.

questions.stem: A notary's paper journal uses numbered pages held loose in a folder. Which format is required?
options: A permanent bound register with numbered pages
questions.explanation: A tangible journal must be permanent, bound and page-numbered.
feedback: Loose pages do not meet the binding requirement.
Correct. All listed physical features matter.
A title does not bind the pages.
The statute permits formats subject to their requirements.

questions.stem: An electronic journal supports silent alteration of completed records. What integrity requirement applies?
options: Only a password chosen by the customer

Only a customer's signature is needed

Challenges to the record or transaction and other lawful remedies

questions.stem: An attorney without a commission or other listed notarial office offers to replace an absent notary solely because of the law license. What does the Maryland FAQ state?

A deadline cannot supply evidence.

That the client can choose an anonymous name

A surname does not establish the witness.

A cover does not match the records.
Fees do not establish sameness.

A course certificate is unrelated to this performance record.
A business card does not record the ceremony.

Correct. Ten years is the regulatory minimum.
Payment does not end retention.

Only at the next customer request

Ask only about the document's title later
Display the record to and have it identified by the principal during recording

feedback: Hiding prevents the required connection.
A sample is not the actual record.
A later discussion does not satisfy the recorded step.

An invoice is not the statutory declaration.
A blank envelope does not identify the record.
Provider terms do not replace the required papers.

feedback: Thirty days exceeds the period.
Correct. Do not import another state's four-day rule.
Renewal is unrelated.
A recipient does not set the statutory deadline.

options: Execute the certificate with the required witnessed-by-technology statement

feedback: The recording must be retained.
A verbal promise does not supply the certificate.
Correct. Follow the receipt and certification sequence.
A blank form does not evidence the act.

Billing is unrelated.
Payroll is unrelated.

options: Other procedures satisfying the statutory same-record requirement
A waiver of all remote duties

Same-record confirmation remains required.
An anonymous email does not automatically satisfy it.

options: An audiovisual recording of the oath with required retention

feedback: A card does not record the ceremony.
Correct. The remote oath has the stated record duties.
An employer note does not replace recording.
A still image is not the audiovisual oath record.

questions.stem: A remote certificate omits the principal's remote participation and communication technology. What statement is required?
options: An indication that a remotely located individual and communication technology were involved

feedback: Price does not state the act method.
Internet-provider identity is not the statutory statement.
Correct. Include the required remote indication.
A phone number does not describe remote participation.

options: The notary cannot be required to use an unselected technology

feedback: The statute limits that demand.
The notary has the statutory selection authority.
Cost does not override selection and compliance.

questions.stem: An electronic-record system is freely editable with no tamper evidence. Which statutory technology characteristic matters?
questions.explanation: Section 18-220(a) authorizes selection of tamper-evident technologies.
feedback: Correct. Integrity is a statutory characteristic.
Screen size does not establish it.
Brand recognition does not establish compliance.
A subscription does not establish tamper evidence.

questions.stem: A provider offers Maryland remote service before receiving state vendor authorization. What does COMAR.05 require?
options: Written authorization before allowing Maryland notaries to use its technology
