feedback: Advertising does not establish state authorization.
Correct. Vendor authorization precedes use.
Payment does not replace approval.
A business card does not establish approval.

questions.stem: An authorized vendor lets a notary subscribe without technology training. What vendor duty was missed?
questions.explanation: COMAR.05 C requires vendor training before services are provided.
feedback: A receipt does not provide training.
Prices do not teach lawful operation.
Correct. The vendor must provide system training.
Client names do not train the notary.

questions.stem: A vendor checks commission status only at initial subscription and ignores later years. What does COMAR require?
options: Check only on a client complaint
Check good standing initially and annually during subscription
questions.explanation: The regulation requires initial and annual good-standing confirmation.
feedback: The rule expressly requires checks.
A complaint is not the sole trigger.
Ten years is too infrequent.
Correct. Maintain annual status checking.

questions.stem: A vendor stores recordings but refuses the notary any access to their own acts. What qualification requirement applies?
options: The vendor must ensure the notary has access to the recordings
Only customers may ever access them
The vendor may erase them immediately
A subscription agreement can eliminate the regulatory requirement
questions.explanation: COMAR.04 B requires notary access to the retained audiovisual records.
feedback: Correct. Storage must support the notary's access.
The rule expressly includes notary access.
The retention minimum prevents immediate erasure.
A private agreement cannot remove the rule.

cards.title: Initial and renewal education
cards.front: How do Maryland's two education routes differ?
cards.rule: Initial applicants complete the authorized course and pass its examination. Renewals require course completion under §18-102.
cards.boundary: One broad FAQ paragraph incorrectly also says renewal exam. The statute and dedicated renewal page preserve the distinction.
cards.mixup: Do not turn a conflicting summary into an extra renewal requirement.

cards.title: Regulatory exam minimum
cards.front: What specifications govern the provider final?
cards.rule: The final contains at least 20 four-choice questions with one correct answer each and requires at least 80%.
cards.boundary: The bank contains at least 50 different questions. A uniform time limit was not verified.
cards.mixup: A minimum count is not an exact statewide question count.

cards.title: Retest opportunity
cards.front: Who qualifies for a provider retest?
cards.rule: An applicant who completed the course but scored below 80% qualifies for an opportunity to retest.
cards.boundary: The provider issues a completion certificate for the course and a passing certificate for successful examination.
cards.mixup: Course attendance does not itself establish an examination pass.

cards.title: Application evidence
cards.front: Which education records accompany the first application?
cards.rule: Submit electronic copies of both the course-completion and examination-passing certificates through the official online route.
cards.boundary: The new-applicant checklist also includes identity/address evidence and three references.
cards.mixup: One certificate should not be assumed to satisfy both distinct records.
cards.source: Maryland Secretary of State new-applicant instructions — Certificate and application instructions

cards.title: Residence and reciprocity
cards.front: Which location facts determine eligibility?
cards.rule: Applicants reside in Maryland or have a place of employment/practice there. A nonresident's home state must provide the statutory reciprocal opportunity.
cards.boundary: Residents use the senatorial district of residence for the appointment process.
cards.mixup: A borrowed address or employer preference cannot replace actual eligibility.

cards.title: Circuit-court qualification
cards.front: What follows an approval notice?
cards.rule: Qualify before the appropriate circuit-court clerk within 30 days after notice and pay the required fees to receive the commission.
cards.boundary: The new term requires the oath again on renewal.
cards.mixup: The application payment receipt is not completion of court qualification.

cards.title: Renewal window
cards.front: When is ordinary renewal available?
cards.rule: The FAQ states 60 days before expiration through 30 days after expiration. Later applicants use the new-commission route.
cards.boundary: Travel during the window can be addressed through advance office contact for instructions.
cards.mixup: Availability of a late filing does not create expired practice authority.
cards.source: Maryland Secretary of State notary FAQs — Renewal timing FAQ

cards.title: Names and changes
cards.front: How should the commissioned identity be maintained?
cards.rule: Use the permitted name matching government photo ID without nicknames or added professional titles. Report covered information changes within 30 days.
cards.boundary: The FAQ offers distinct name-change options. A newly named replacement commission retains the existing expiration date.
cards.mixup: A name update does not automatically create a fresh four-year term.
cards.source: Maryland Secretary of State notary FAQs — Name and information-change FAQ

cards.title: Active personal email
cards.front: Which contact channel needs continuing attention?
cards.rule: Maintain a current active personal email with the Secretary. COMAR uses email communications except the stated enforcement correspondence.
cards.boundary: Listed email, phone, address and county changes have 30-day notice duties.
cards.mixup: An inactive former employer account should not be the only route for state communications.

cards.title: Dealings and reasonable certainty
cards.front: What establishes statutory personal knowledge?
cards.rule: The officer personally knows the appearing person through dealings sufficient to provide reasonable certainty of the claimed identity.
cards.boundary: Name recognition alone is not the statutory dealings relationship.
cards.mixup: Another person's familiarity does not automatically become the officer's knowledge.

cards.title: Maryland credential categories
cards.front: Which ID categories does §18-206 list?
cards.rule: Passport, driver's license, consular identification or government nondriver card are listed. Other government ID must contain both signature and photograph and be satisfactory.
cards.boundary: Additional assurance may be required.
cards.mixup: Do not import Maine's signature-or-photo alternative into Maryland.

cards.title: Witness identity and solemnity
cards.front: What supports the credible-witness route?
cards.rule: The credible witness appears and verifies on oath or affirmation, with the witness known or identified by the listed credentials.
cards.boundary: Remote witness participation follows the applicable remote provisions.
cards.mixup: A casual introduction or unsworn text does not perform verification.

cards.title: Concurrent directed signing
cards.front: How does §18-208 accommodate physical inability?
cards.rule: The principal appears and directs someone other than the officer who concurrently appears to sign the principal's name.
cards.boundary: Insert the prescribed or similar statement naming the directed signer and principal.
cards.mixup: The helper appearing alone does not satisfy the stated method.

cards.title: Capacity and coercion
cards.front: Which judgments are separate from ID?
cards.rule: The officer may refuse if unsatisfied about competence/capacity or knowing voluntary execution, unless otherwise prohibited by law.
cards.boundary: The customer can be identified yet still show coercion or incapacity concerns.
cards.mixup: An employer's deadline does not determine the signer's free choice.

cards.title: Representative acknowledgment
cards.front: What does the representative declare?
cards.rule: The individual declares proper authority and execution as the represented person's or entity's act.
cards.boundary: The appearing representative's identity and signature connection remain required.
cards.mixup: The notary does not become the representative or guarantee the entity's obligations.

cards.title: Actual ceremony and certificate
cards.front: What does a verification certificate evidence?
cards.rule: Verification requires an actual oath or affirmation declaration. A certificate records the completed act with truthful date, jurisdiction, title, signature and expiration.
cards.boundary: The officer signs in the manner filed with the circuit-court clerk.
cards.mixup: Printed sworn wording does not itself administer an oath.

cards.title: Electronic source to paper
cards.front: What safeguards precede accurate-printout certification?
cards.rule: Reasonably determine tamper-evident format and personally print or supervise printing. Do not certify if a change or error in signature or information is detected.
cards.boundary: The copy must also be full, true and accurate.
cards.mixup: A matching file title does not cure missing pages or an integrity defect.

cards.title: All acts recorded
cards.front: Which acts belong in the Maryland journal?
cards.rule: Chronicle all notarial acts, including free, in-person, electronic and remote service.
cards.boundary: Make each entry contemporaneously.
cards.mixup: A video recording does not replace the separate journal.

cards.title: Journal number and format
cards.front: How are tangible and electronic journals arranged?
cards.rule: Use one at a time for tangible-record acts and one or more for electronic-record acts. Tangible journals are bound permanent registers with numbered pages.
cards.boundary: Electronic journals are permanent and tamper-evident under regulations.
cards.mixup: A separate active book for every office is not the tangible-record arrangement.

cards.title: Required transaction detail
cards.front: Which core facts preserve the act?
cards.rule: Record date/time, record description and act type, individual's full name/address, identity basis, fee and appearance mode.
cards.boundary: The appearance mode distinguishes physical from communication-technology participation.
cards.mixup: Monthly totals do not provide the required individual chronicle.

cards.title: Credential number requirement
cards.front: What Maryland-specific ID detail does COMAR add?
cards.rule: When using a credential under the cited ordinary or remote identity provisions, document its associated identification number in the journal.
cards.boundary: Also record the statutory credential description and issuance/expiration dates.
cards.mixup: Another state's ID-number prohibition should not be applied to Maryland.

cards.title: Actual identity basis
cards.front: How is personal knowledge distinguished in the entry?
cards.rule: State that personal knowledge was the basis when used. For satisfactory evidence, describe the actual method and credential details.
cards.boundary: Do not invent an ID inspection that did not occur.
cards.mixup: A generic known label should reflect the true statutory relationship.

cards.title: Retention anchor
cards.front: When does the journal's ten-year clock begin?
cards.rule: Retain the journal ten years after the last act chronicled.
cards.boundary: The first page, purchase date and employment end do not control.
cards.mixup: A recently used old volume is not ready for disposal based on its age alone.

cards.title: Loss and cessation
cards.front: What happens after loss or leaving office?
cards.rule: Promptly notify the Secretary after discovering journal loss/theft. On resignation, revocation or suspension, retain and report the location, subject to approved alternatives.
cards.boundary: A current or former officer may use the approved repository or regulatory storage alternative.
cards.mixup: The end of a commission does not authorize erasing its history.

cards.title: Successor custody
cards.front: Who acts after death or incompetency?
cards.rule: The representative, guardian or knowing possessor follows the approved repository/storage disposition in §18-219(g).
cards.boundary: The separate recording-successor notice rule may also apply to remote records.
cards.mixup: An arbitrary storage company is not automatically an approved repository.

cards.title: Ordinary and remote ceilings
cards.front: What current act-fee limits apply?
cards.rule: The maximum is $8 for an original ordinary notarial act and $30 for a remote act.
cards.boundary: The regulation permits charging up to the ceiling rather than mandating the full charge.
cards.mixup: Changing a label does not authorize an excessive notarial fee.

cards.title: Additional-copy condition
cards.front: When does the $4 additional-copy rate apply?
cards.rule: The same record's copies must be signed at the same time by the same person or persons. The first-copy rule permits $8 per signature and additional copies $4 per signature.
cards.boundary: The full same-record, same-time, same-person conditions matter.
cards.mixup: A later appointment is not automatically an additional copy under this special rule.

cards.title: Reproduction and certification
cards.front: Which copy services have separate rates?
cards.rule: Mere reproduction of a notarized record or journal entry is capped at $2 per furnished copy. Certifying a journal-record copy may cost $6.
cards.boundary: Identify the actual requested service.
cards.mixup: A photocopy and a certified journal copy are distinct fee categories.

cards.title: Travel compensation
cards.front: What two travel components are allowed?
cards.rule: The regulation allows the prevailing IRS business-travel mileage reimbursement and a separate travel fee not exceeding $5.
cards.boundary: Verify the applicable current external mileage rate for the trip.
cards.mixup: The $5 ceiling is not a per-mile rate.

cards.title: Stamp identity
cards.front: What official identity belongs on the seal?
cards.rule: The stamp identifies the notary's name and office and required county information, and must be reproducible with the record.
cards.boundary: A nonresident uses the Maryland qualification county. Expiration may be in the stamp or certificate under §18-217(b).
cards.mixup: A company logo cannot replace the commissioned individual's official information.

cards.title: Paper stamp duty
cards.front: Which ordinary paper act requires an official impression?
cards.rule: A notary public performing an act on a tangible record affixes or embosses the official stamp on the certificate.
cards.boundary: The statute separately uses may for an electronic-record officer's stamp association, with other standards applicable.
cards.mixup: Do not import another state's optional ordinary-paper stamp rule.

cards.title: Personal device control
cards.front: Who may use the stamping device?
cards.rule: The commissioned notary keeps security and cannot allow another individual to use the device for an act.
cards.boundary: Employer payment does not transfer the stamp's personal ownership or responsibility.
cards.mixup: A trusted receptionist cannot cover appointments with another person's seal.
cards.source: Maryland State Government §18-218 — §18-218(a)(1); employer-paid stamp FAQ

cards.title: Device exit and loss
cards.front: What ends a device's usable life?
cards.rule: On the statutory resignation, revocation, commission/device expiration events, render it unusable. Promptly report loss or theft.
cards.boundary: A responsible possessor has disabling duties after death or incompetency.
cards.mixup: Simply hiding a still-usable stamp does not necessarily achieve disabling.

cards.title: Certificate location and association
cards.front: How do official details stay connected to the record?
cards.rule: Use actual act date and jurisdiction, official filed-manner signature, title and expiration. Securely attach a paper certificate or logically associate an electronic one.
cards.boundary: The act precedes execution of its certificate.
cards.mixup: A fee receipt or detached reusable form does not replace the completed certificate.

cards.title: Notary and spouse conflict
cards.front: Which interests create the mandatory record conflict?
cards.rule: Do not act on a record to which the notary or spouse is a party or in which either has a direct beneficial interest.
cards.boundary: A violating act is voidable.
cards.mixup: An unrelated appearing signer does not erase a spouse's record interest.

cards.title: Broader family recommendation
cards.front: How should immediate-family caution be described?
cards.rule: The FAQ recommends refraining for immediate family and personal involvement beyond the statute's stated mandatory conflicts.
cards.boundary: Keep the recommendation distinct from a claimed categorical statutory ban.
cards.mixup: Another state's broader family prohibition is not Maryland's §18-203 text.
cards.source: Maryland Secretary of State notary FAQs — Family notarization FAQ

cards.title: Application and advertising honesty
cards.front: What misrepresentations may support discipline?
cards.rule: Dishonest application statements/omissions and false claims of notarial duties, rights or privileges are listed grounds under §18-104.
cards.boundary: Adverse notary action by another state is also listed.
cards.mixup: A private advertisement cannot create missing public authority.

cards.title: Covered conviction notice
cards.front: When is a covered conviction reported?
cards.rule: COMAR requires notice within ten days after conviction or release from incarceration, whichever is later.
cards.boundary: The provision covers the specified felony/fraud/dishonesty/deceit convictions.
cards.mixup: Waiting until the next renewal can miss the deadline.

cards.title: Professional license limits
cards.front: Does a law or other professional license automatically confer Maryland notarial office?
cards.rule: The FAQ requires actual status as a statutorily authorized notarial officer.
cards.boundary: Section 18-209 lists notaries and the specified court officers.
cards.mixup: An attorney license alone is not a blanket substitute for an absent notary.

cards.title: Territorial authority
cards.front: Where may the Maryland commission be used?
cards.rule: The officer is physically in Maryland and may act throughout the state regardless of commissioning county.
cards.boundary: A document may be intended for use elsewhere.
cards.mixup: The customer's residence or record destination does not relocate the officer.
cards.source: Maryland Secretary of State notary FAQs — Statewide authority and location FAQ

cards.title: Validity and other remedies
cards.front: What does a valid act leave unresolved?
cards.rule: Section 18-221 preserves other-law challenges to the record/transaction and other remedies. It does not validate acts by people without authority.
cards.boundary: Commission discipline also does not foreclose other lawful remedies.
cards.mixup: A seal is not a guarantee that the transaction cannot be challenged.

cards.title: Two notification routes
cards.front: Which remote categories can be selected?
cards.rule: The online form permits electronic-record RON using an authorized vendor and/or other-technology remote acts.
cards.boundary: Select the actual route and complete the official authorization process.
cards.mixup: A generic video subscription alone does not authorize remote service.
cards.source: Maryland Secretary of State remote-notary instructions — Remote authorization instructions

cards.title: Alternative identity route
cards.front: What supports remote service without analysis and proofing?
cards.rule: The special form acknowledges personal knowledge or the qualifying appearing credible-witness verification route.
cards.boundary: The documentary remote route combines presentation, credential analysis and identity proofing.
cards.mixup: Omitting automated components does not remove identity requirements.

cards.title: Surroundings and participants
cards.front: What must the remote technology capture?
cards.rule: It must support an audiovisual record of the entire physical location and all persons physically present. Those persons identify themselves and their roles.
cards.boundary: The notary still confirms the same record and actual ceremony.
cards.mixup: A pen closeup alone omits the broader location/person requirement.

cards.title: Tangible declaration deadline
cards.front: What is Maryland's specified tangible declaration deadline?
cards.rule: The principal signs the record and attached/integrated declaration during recording and sends both no later than three days after the act.
cards.boundary: The officer certifies after receipt, and a compliant act is effective on the declaration date. Other qualifying procedures are preserved.
cards.mixup: Do not substitute another state's four-day transmission period.

cards.title: Officer and abroad principal
cards.front: Which geographic conditions govern?
cards.rule: The officer is in Maryland. An abroad principal needs the statutory United States nexus, and the officer must have no actual knowledge of foreign prohibition.
cards.boundary: The record's destination does not move the officer.
cards.mixup: An approved platform cannot cure an officer's out-of-state physical location.

cards.title: Ten-year recording record
cards.front: What survives the session?
cards.rule: Create and retain the remote audiovisual recording for at least ten years and include the remote-method certificate statement.
cards.boundary: A successor assuming recording authority notifies the Secretary within 30 days under the statute.
cards.mixup: The journal is additional to the recording.

cards.title: Vendor and renewal changes
cards.front: What keeps remote authorization current?
cards.rule: Notify a new vendor within ten business days, promptly report a vendor compliance concern, and submit a new remote notification on renewal.
cards.boundary: Remote authority expires with the ordinary commission and may be canceled by written notice.
cards.mixup: An active vendor subscription does not extend an expired commission.

cards.title: Vendor obligations
cards.front: Which protections must a vendor provide?
cards.rule: The vendor is state-authorized, provides technology training, checks notary good standing initially and annually, and supports ten-year recording retention with notary access.
cards.boundary: COMAR also imposes the stated information-security and breach-notice duties.
cards.mixup: A vendor invoice does not establish authorization or replace the notary's duties.

cards.title: Selected technology and printouts
cards.front: Which electronic-record controls matter?
cards.rule: The notary selects qualifying tamper-evident technology and cannot be compelled to use an unselected one. Accurate tangible copies follow the printing/integrity requirements.
cards.boundary: Section 18-220's recording provision has stated conditions and a plat exclusion.
cards.mixup: A record's electronic format does not guarantee every printed copy's eligibility.

commission.summary: Maryland first applicants complete authorized education and examination before online filing and court qualification. Renewal requires the course and a fresh court oath.

sections.heading: Complete the appropriate education
sections.body: Section 18-102 requires initial course completion and examination passing. Current COMAR requires at least 20 four-choice questions with one correct answer, at least 80% correct and a bank of at least 50 questions. A qualified course completer who fails receives a retest opportunity. Uniform exam timing was not verified. Renewal requires the course under the statute and dedicated renewal instructions, despite an inconsistent general FAQ eligibility paragraph.

sections.heading: Apply and qualify in the proper place
sections.body: Residents use the home address and senatorial district of residence. Qualifying nonresidents have Maryland employment/practice and satisfy the home-state reciprocity condition. First applications include the completion and passing certificates, required ID/address evidence and three reference contacts. After approval, qualify before the appropriate circuit-court clerk within 30 days after notice and pay the prescribed fees to receive the commission. The term is four years.

sections.heading: Maintain the commission record
sections.body: The ordinary renewal window is 60 days before through 30 days after expiration. Later applicants use the new-commission route. A new commission requires the court oath again. Report listed name, address, email, phone and county changes within 30 days and keep a current active personal email with the Secretary. The FAQ provides name-change options and explains that a replacement under a new name retains the current expiration.

example.heading: A first applicant's two certificates
example.body: An applicant finishes the course and receives its completion certificate, then passes the examination and receives the passing certificate. Both are uploaded with the first application. The application-payment email is followed by review and the court-qualification instructions. The applicant completes those steps before using the commission.

keyFacts: Initial education includes course and examination. Renewal requires the course.
The examination has a minimum 20 questions and at least 80% passing.
Uniform examination timing remains unverified.
Court qualification is due within 30 days after notice.
Keep the required personal email and commission information current.

identification.summary: Maryland identity evidence supports identifying the actual appearing individual. Capacity, voluntary execution, the ceremony and the certificate remain separate requirements.

sections.heading: Establish the identity basis
sections.body: Personal knowledge rests on dealings sufficient to provide reasonable certainty. The statute lists passport, driver's license, consular identification and government nondriver card. The alternative government-ID category contains both signature and photograph and is satisfactory to the officer. An appearing credible witness verifies on oath or affirmation and is known or credential-identified under the listed methods. Additional information may be required to assure identity.

sections.heading: Support lawful participation
sections.body: Section 18-208 permits a physically unable principal to direct another individual other than the officer who appears concurrently to sign. Insert the required or similar direction statement. Section 18-207 permits refusal when the officer is unsatisfied of competence/capacity or knowing voluntary signing, unless otherwise prohibited by law. An identity card does not settle whether a companion is coercing the principal.

sections.heading: Connect the actual act and certificate
sections.body: Acknowledgment and verification require the identity and signature determinations specified in §18-204. Verification includes the actual oath/affirmation declaration. Representative acknowledgment includes proper authority and execution as the represented party's act. The certificate is contemporaneous, signed in the filed manner, dated and given the required jurisdiction, title and expiration. Securely attach a tangible certificate or logically associate an electronic one. The act precedes certificate execution.

example.heading: A concurrent helper
example.body: A principal physically unable to sign appears with an assistant and directs that person to affix the name. The notary completes the lawful participation and identity checks, uses the required directed-signature statement and performs the requested act. An assistant arriving alone would leave the principal's concurrent appearance missing.

keyFacts: The alternative government-ID category requires signature and photograph.
Credible witnesses give actual oath/affirmation verification.
The officer can request additional identity assurance.
Directed signers appear concurrently with the principal.
The certificate describes the actual ceremony and act location.

journals.summary: Maryland journals chronicle all acts. Record them contemporaneously with the statute's fields and COMAR's credential-number requirement.

sections.heading: Record every act with the right information
sections.body: Journal free and paid, in-person, electronic and remote acts. Each entry contains date/time, record description and act type, individual's full name/address, identity basis, fee and physical/remote appearance mode. State personal knowledge when used. For satisfactory evidence, describe the method and credential with issuance/expiration dates. COMAR.08 C adds the associated identification number for credentials used under the cited ordinary and remote provisions.

sections.heading: Use the statutory format and arrangement
sections.body: Maintain only one journal at a time for tangible-record acts and one or more for electronic-record acts. A tangible journal is a permanent bound register with numbered pages. An electronic journal is permanent and tamper-evident under applicable regulations. An audiovisual recording does not replace the journal. A monthly summary does not provide the required contemporaneous individual entries.

sections.heading: Retain and locate records after office
sections.body: Retention runs ten years after the journal's last act. Promptly report loss or theft. On resignation, revocation or suspension, retain and inform the Secretary of location, subject to transfer to an approved repository or approved regulatory storage. The representative, guardian or knowing possessor follows the statutory disposition after death or incompetency. Actual approval of the storage route matters.

example.heading: A credential-based remote entry
example.body: A notary identifies a remote principal through the lawful documentary process. The entry records the actual method, credential details and associated number required by COMAR, as well as the remote appearance mode and other fields. The performance recording is separately preserved under the remote rules.

keyFacts: Every act is journaled, including free service.
COMAR requires the associated credential identification number.
Record appearance mode as well as identity method.
Ten-year retention uses the last act in that journal.
Approved repositories and regulatory storage provide specified alternatives.

seals-fees.summary: Current Maryland fee ceilings depend on the actual service. Official stamp identity, device security and certificate execution each require attention.

sections.heading: Classify the charge
sections.body: COMAR.02 caps an original ordinary act at $8 and a remote act at $30. The same-record copies signed at the same time by the same person or persons permit $8 per first-copy signature and $4 per additional-copy signature. Mere reproductions are capped at $2 per furnished copy, and certification of a journal-record copy may cost $6. Travel may include the prevailing IRS business-travel mileage reimbursement and a fee not exceeding $5.

sections.heading: Use a compliant official impression
sections.body: The stamp identifies the notary's name and office with required county information and can be copied with its record. A nonresident uses the qualification county. Expiration can be in the stamp or certificate under §18-217(b). A notary public's tangible-record certificate receives the official affixed or embossed stamp. The statute separately uses may for an electronic-record officer's stamp association, subject to applicable standards.

sections.heading: Protect the device through its lifecycle
sections.body: The notary remains responsible for security and cannot allow another person's use. Employer payment does not transfer the stamp's personal ownership or custody. On the statutory resignation, revocation and expiration events, disable the device so it is unusable. Promptly notify the Secretary after loss or theft. The responsible possessor has disabling duties following death or incompetency.

example.heading: Two requested copy services
example.body: One requester asks for a plain reproduction of a journal entry and another asks for a certified copy of a journal record. The notary identifies the actual service before applying the $2 reproduction limit or $6 certification charge. Calling every copy a remote act would misclassify the service and its fee.

keyFacts: Current original ordinary and remote ceilings are $8 and $30.
The special additional-copy rule requires all stated same-time conditions.
Verify the prevailing IRS mileage rate instead of assuming a historical figure.
The stamp is personal to the commissioned officer.
Tangible certificates performed by a notary public require the official stamp.

prohibited-acts.summary: The mandatory conflict rule concerns the notary and spouse's party status or direct beneficial interests. Official broader family caution is separately identified.

sections.heading: Screen actual statutory interests
sections.body: Section 18-203 bars an act on a record to which the notary or spouse is a party or in which either has a direct beneficial interest. A violation is voidable. The FAQ recommends refraining for immediate family and indirect personal involvement beyond the stated duty. Ordinary employment by a corporation does not automatically establish a prohibited personal interest under the FAQ's described nonparty situation.

sections.heading: Respect authority and honesty
sections.body: Dishonest applications, misleading claims of public authority and adverse other-state notary action are statutory discipline grounds. COMAR includes identity, certificate, fee, journal and remote-notice failures among enforcement examples. A professional license alone does not supply notarial authority. Maryland acts occur while the officer is physically in Maryland, with statewide authority regardless of commissioning county.

sections.heading: Preserve the statutory limits on validity
sections.body: Section 18-221 does not validate acts by persons without authority and preserves challenges to the underlying record/transaction and other lawful remedies. Commission discipline also does not foreclose other civil/criminal remedies. A covered conviction has the specific COMAR reporting period. The FAQ permits denying illegal, improper or known fraudulent requests and confines the notarial role in a customer's document to its proper certificate.

example.heading: A spouse's interest with an unrelated customer
example.body: An unrelated seller appears with a record in which the notary's spouse is a party. The notary applies the record-based conflict, not just the appearing person's relationship. Another authorized officer is needed. A fee waiver and complete journal would not remove that statutory interest.

keyFacts: Check both notary and spouse's party/direct-benefit interests.
A conflicting act is voidable.
Broader immediate-family caution is a recommendation in the FAQ.
Professional licensure alone does not create notarial office.
A valid notarization does not settle all transaction challenges.

electronic-ron.summary: Maryland remote service uses the official notification route matching the intended record and technology. State approval, identity, recording and continuing notification duties apply.

sections.heading: Authorize the intended route
sections.body: The online form permits selecting electronic-record RON using an authorized vendor and/or other-technology remote acts. The route without credential analysis/identity proofing requires the personal-knowledge or qualifying credible-witness foundation in COMAR.07 A(3). For the documentary route, §18-214 combines credential presentation, analysis and identity proofing. Vendor changes have ten-business-day notice;renewal requires a new remote notification.

sections.heading: Control the session and location
sections.body: The notary is physically in Maryland and confirms the same record. Abroad principals need the statutory United States connection and no actual knowledge by the notary of foreign prohibition. COMAR requires technology capable of recording the entire physical location and all persons physically present, and those people identify themselves and their roles. Create and retain the audiovisual performance record at least ten years.

sections.heading: Complete the tangible and certificate steps
sections.body: The statutory tangible declaration method requires the principal to sign both record and integrated/securely attached declaration during recording and send them within three days. The officer executes the certificate after receipt, and the compliant act is effective on the declaration date. The statute preserves other qualifying same-record procedures. The certificate indicates the remotely located individual and communication technology. Successors assuming recording authority have thirty-day state notice.

example.heading: A replacement remote vendor
example.body: A notary selects a new authorized vendor, completes its required training and reports the change within ten business days. If the selected system appears unable to comply, the notary promptly reports the problem. An active subscription does not extend remote authority past commission expiration, and renewal requires the new remote notification.

keyFacts: Select the actual electronic-vendor and/or other-technology route.
The documentary identity method contains three components.
Record the required surroundings and identify physically present people.
Maryland's specified tangible declaration method sends papers within three days.
Remote authority expires with the ordinary commission.

articles.keyword: Maryland notary examination minimum questions passing
articles.title: Maryland Provider Finals and Retest Standards
articles.description: Read the verified minimum count, passing threshold, question bank and retest provisions.
articles.lede: Maryland regulates the provider's examination design. Minimum counts and separate certificates matter when judging whether an advertised assessment meets the rules.

sections.heading: Read minimum as minimum
sections.body: COMAR 01.02.08.16 F requires an examination containing at least twenty multiple-choice questions. It does not establish a universal exact twenty-question count. Each question has four answers and one correct choice. Consider a provider advertising a final shorter than twenty questions. The minimum-count rule is directly relevant. A provider administering more questions is evaluated under the full standards rather than rejected solely for exceeding the minimum.

sections.heading: Distinguish the bank from the administered final
sections.body: Regulation.16 E requires a robust bank of at least fifty different questions so repeat applicants do not receive a statistically sufficient number of previously attempted items. This bank is distinct from the number presented in an individual session. A learner should therefore identify whether a figure concerns stored items or the actual examination. The regulation also calls for comparable difficulty and coverage of handbook laws, regulations, ethics and procedures.

sections.heading: Separate completion from passing
sections.body: Regulation.15 requires a course-completion certificate and a passing certificate for an examination score of at least eighty percent. The new-applicant instructions require electronic copies of both records. A first applicant who has only attended the course has not yet supplied the separate examination result. Renewal follows the course requirement in section 18-102 and the dedicated renewal page, with the inconsistent broad FAQ paragraph disclosed as a source discrepancy.

sections.heading: Use the retest and scoring provisions
sections.body: A course completer who scores below eighty percent qualifies for an opportunity to retest under regulation.15 E. Regulation.16 I requires immediate scoring at the conclusion of the session. The opened provisions do not establish a uniform examination clock, and this learning pack does not invent one. An applicant should use the authorized provider's current instructions for delivery arrangements while checking that the regulatory result and certificate requirements are met.

sources.title: Maryland Secretary of State new-applicant instructions

faqs.q: Is every Maryland final exactly twenty questions?
faqs.a: The regulation requires at least twenty questions.

faqs.q: What passing threshold is verified?
faqs.a: COMAR requires at least eighty percent correct for the Certificate of Passing.

articles.title: Maryland's Credential Number Belongs in the Journal
articles.description: Connect statutory identification descriptions with COMAR's additional number requirement.
articles.lede: The statutory journal field list and the general responsibilities regulation work together. Read both before configuring a journal template.

sections.heading: Begin with the statutory fields
sections.body: Section 18-219(c) requires a contemporaneous entry including the identity basis. When satisfactory evidence is used, the notary briefly describes the method and credential, including its issuance and expiration dates. The entry also identifies the individual, record, act, date/time, fee and appearance mode. A template that captures only a client's initials and a generic checked-ID mark would omit several of these required facts.

sections.heading: Apply the regulation's express addition
sections.body: COMAR 01.02.08.08 C requires the identification number associated with a credential used under the cited ordinary and remote identity provisions. This supplies the legal basis for the number field also listed in the official FAQ. A notary who has worked in another state should check Maryland's actual rule before disabling that field. The legal question is the requirement governing the Maryland act and the credential actually used.

sections.heading: Record the actual method
sections.body: Personal knowledge has a separate statutory journal statement. The notary should not invent a credential inspection when the identity basis was genuine personal knowledge. Conversely, an actual credential-based method requires the applicable credential details and number. For remote witness or documentary methods, the regulation's cited provisions must be considered. Accurate method selection makes the journal a usable account of what supported this individual's identity at this act.

sections.heading: Preserve the whole transaction record
sections.body: The journal also indicates whether appearance was physical or through communication technology. Remote recordings are additional records with their own retention rules. A recording does not make the journal's identity fields optional, and an elaborate journal does not remove the separate remote recording duty. The notary preserves these records through the statutory format and retention requirements, with an accurate contemporaneous entry for the actual performed act.

sources.title: Maryland Secretary of State notary FAQs

faqs.q: Does Maryland COMAR require the associated credential number?
faqs.a: Yes. Regulation.08 C requires it for credentials used under the cited identity provisions.

faqs.q: Does a remote recording replace the journal entry?
faqs.a: The journal and audiovisual recording are separate required records.

articles.keyword: Maryland notary spouse beneficial interest family
articles.intent: Separate mandatory conflicts and official recommendations
articles.title: Maryland Spouse Interests and Broader Family Guidance
articles.description: Apply the record-based statutory conflict and preserve the FAQ's recommendation status.
articles.lede: A record can create a prohibited spouse interest even when an unrelated person appears. The FAQ also gives broader family guidance with a different stated status.

sections.heading: Screen record parties
sections.body: Section 18-203(b) bars the notarial act if the notary or spouse is a party to the record. Imagine an unrelated seller bringing an instrument that names the notary's spouse as a transaction party. The seller's identity and lack of family relationship do not remove that record fact. The officer should examine the statutory involvement before taking the act, with another authorized officer handling a disqualified transaction.

sections.heading: Examine direct beneficial interests
sections.body: The same subsection independently addresses the notary's or spouse's direct beneficial interest. An officer need not be named as a party for a direct personal benefit to matter. A complete journal, lawful fee or correct seal does not waive the conflict. The record-interest review therefore belongs alongside the identity and ceremony checks, with the officer avoiding an act that the statute prohibits before executing its certificate.

sections.heading: Preserve the broader recommendation
sections.body: The FAQ recommends refraining for immediate family and for matters involving the officer personally, even where the stated legal duty may not require refusal. That advice should remain visible without being rewritten as a categorical statutory ban on every sibling or parent act. The learner should identify both the mandatory notary/spouse party-or-direct-interest rule and the broader official recommendation when assessing a proposed family appointment.

sections.heading: Use the consequence and validity rules precisely
sections.body: Section 18-203 describes a violating act as voidable. Section 18-221's general validity provision expressly preserves that conflict rule and other-law challenges to the underlying record or transaction. These provisions should not be used as permission to take a prohibited act. They describe legal consequences and retained remedies. Employer pressure and a customer's waiver do not expand the officer's authority over a conflicted record.

sources.title: Maryland Secretary of State notary FAQs

faqs.q: Can an unrelated signer still present a spouse conflict?
faqs.a: Yes. The spouse's party status or direct beneficial interest in the record independently matters.

faqs.q: Is the FAQ's immediate-family advice a blanket statutory prohibition?
faqs.a: The FAQ presents broader refraining guidance as a recommendation beyond the stated statutory duty.

articles.keyword: Maryland physically unable sign concurrent appearance
articles.title: Concurrent Appearance for Maryland Directed Signatures
articles.description: Apply section 18-208 while preserving identity, voluntary direction and certificate accuracy.
articles.h1: A Maryland Appointment with a Directed Signer
articles.lede: Physical inability to write can be addressed through the statutory directed-signature procedure. The principal remains an active participant in the appointment.

sections.heading: Establish the principal's direction
sections.body: Section 18-208 applies when the individual is physically unable to sign a record. The individual appears and directs another individual other than the notarial officer to sign the individual's name. Consider a principal with a hand injury accompanied by an assistant. The direction comes from the principal. The officer should not treat the assistant's convenience or an employer's instruction as a substitute for the principal's participation.

sections.heading: Require concurrent appearance
sections.body: The statute requires the directed signer to appear concurrently with the principal before the officer. An assistant arriving alone with a letter and a copy of the principal's identification leaves that stated method incomplete. Appearance and identification should be handled under the applicable act provisions. A person's physical inability to affix a signature does not eliminate the need for the principal's lawful appearance and the required determinations.

sections.heading: Insert the execution statement
sections.body: Section 18-208(b) requires the prescribed or similar words identifying who affixed the signature and at whose direction. The statement explains the actual execution method on the record. It is separate from selecting and performing the requested acknowledgment, verification or other act. A certificate or notation should not falsely suggest the officer personally signed the principal's name, which the directed-signer provision expressly excludes.

sections.heading: Assess knowing and voluntary participation
sections.body: Section 18-207 permits refusal when the officer is not satisfied of competence/capacity or knowing voluntary signing, unless otherwise prohibited by law. A principal can have an identified assistant while still appearing coerced or unable to understand the execution. The officer's role is to make the required judgments about the actual participant and ceremony. Complete the certificate only after the lawful act and preserve the required journal information.

faqs.q: May the notarial officer act as the directed signer?
faqs.a: Section 18-208 specifies another individual other than the notarial officer.

faqs.q: Can the assistant appear without the principal?
faqs.a: The statutory method requires concurrent appearance with the principal.

articles.keyword: Maryland notary additional copy travel fee
articles.title: Maryland Copy and Travel Charges Need Classification
articles.description: Distinguish ordinary, remote, additional-copy, reproduction, certification and travel fees.
articles.lede: Several lawful services can occur around one appointment. The actual service and the regulation's conditions determine the applicable fee treatment.

sections.heading: Identify the original act category
sections.body: COMAR 01.02.08.02 A permits no more than eight dollars for an original ordinary act or thirty dollars for a remote act. These are maxima, the notary may charge within the lawful limit. Calling the same excessive notarial charge a convenience fee does not change what service was performed. The journal records the actual fee, and recording an excessive charge does not itself make that charge lawful.

sections.heading: Apply the additional-copy conditions
sections.body: Regulation.02 B addresses multiple copies of the same record signed at the same time by the same person or persons. It permits eight dollars per signature on the original or first copy and four dollars per signature on additional copies. A client returning the next week with another copy does not automatically meet the same-time condition. The notary should identify the complete stated transaction facts before using this special fee treatment.

sections.heading: Distinguish reproduction and certification
sections.body: Regulation.02 C limits a requested reproduction of a notarized record or journal entry to two dollars per furnished copy. Regulation.02 E permits six dollars for certifying a copy of a record in the journal. A plain photocopy and a certified journal-record copy are different services. The requester and notary should identify what is actually being supplied so the office does not treat every copying request as a new remote act.

sections.heading: Calculate travel under its own rule
sections.body: Regulation.02 D permits mileage reimbursement at the prevailing IRS business-travel rate and a travel fee not exceeding five dollars. The five-dollar limit is a separate travel component rather than a per-mile rate. Because the regulation references a prevailing external rate, the applicable current figure should be verified for the actual trip. A historical notebook entry or vendor's marketing suggestion should not silently become the incorporated rate.

faqs.q: When does the four-dollar additional-copy rate apply?
faqs.a: The same record's copies must be signed at the same time by the same person or persons under the regulation.

faqs.q: Is five dollars the mileage rate?
faqs.a: It is the separate travel-fee ceiling. Mileage uses the prevailing IRS business-travel rate.

articles.keyword: Maryland notary stamp employer custody expiration
articles.intent: Protect the device across employment changes
articles.title: The Maryland Stamp Remains a Personal Responsibility
articles.description: Follow personal control, loss notice and statutory disabling duties.
articles.h1: Managing a Maryland Stamping Device through Office Changes
articles.lede: Employer purchase does not make an individual notary's stamping device a shared office tool. Security duties continue during storage and at the end of authority.

sections.heading: Keep personal control despite reimbursement
sections.body: Section 18-218 makes each notary responsible for device security and prohibits allowing another person to use it for an act. The FAQ adds that the official stamp belongs to the notary alone even if the employer bought it. A receptionist therefore cannot cover a notary's lunch break with that person's stamp. The employer's expenditure and trust in the receptionist do not transfer the commissioned individual's public authority.

sections.heading: Preserve the correct official identity
sections.body: Section 18-217 requires the notary's name and office with appropriate county information and reproducibility with the record. For a nonresident, the qualification county is specified. The commission expiration can be in the stamp or certificate under subsection(b). These are official details rather than decorative branding. A company logo or unrelated county does not replace the individual officer's required identification.

sections.heading: Report loss promptly
sections.body: Loss or theft triggers prompt notice to the Secretary upon discovery. The FAQ describes information for the email notice, including the commissioned name, address, county and date of loss or theft, and permits police-report information where available. The duty does not depend on proof that someone already forged a record. The notary should treat discovery of the missing device as the event requiring state notice.

sections.heading: Render the device unusable at the required events
sections.body: The statute requires disabling after resignation, revocation, commission expiration or expiration of the device's stated date. The listed methods must make the device unusable. After death or adjudicated incompetency, the responsible representative, guardian or knowing possessor has the disabling duty. An unlocked drawer or usable sale to a coworker does not achieve the specified result merely because the former officer no longer intends to use the stamp.

sources.title: Maryland Secretary of State notary FAQs

faqs.q: Does employer payment allow another employee to use the stamp?
faqs.a: No. The notary retains personal responsibility and may not allow another individual's use for an act.

faqs.q: When is loss reported?
faqs.a: Promptly after discovering the device was lost or stolen.

articles.keyword: Maryland tangible copy electronic record printing
articles.title: Maryland Paper Copies of Electronic Records
articles.description: Review tamper evidence, supervised printing, detected errors and recording conditions.
articles.h1: Certifying a Tangible Maryland Electronic-Record Copy
articles.lede: An accurate paper copy of an electronic instrument has a specific statutory procedure. The officer's supervision and integrity determinations are part of the act.

sections.heading: Check the electronic source's integrity
sections.body: Section 18-204(e) requires the officer to reasonably determine whether the electronic record is in a tamper-evident format. This is more than confirming that a file opens on a screen. Suppose a requester supplies an electronic instrument intended for a paper recording submission. The officer examines the actual source under the statutory condition before treating its printout as an accurate tangible copy.

sections.heading: Control the printing process
sections.body: The same provision requires personally printing or supervising printing onto paper or another tangible medium. A customer-supplied printout and a statement that it is correct do not automatically establish that the officer performed this required step. The officer also determines the reproduction is full, true and accurate. Missing pages, tables or other substantive content should be resolved before executing a certificate describing an accurate copy.

sections.heading: Stop on a detected change or error
sections.body: The statute prohibits making the certification if the officer detects a change or error in an electronic signature or other information in the electronic record. A matching title or the customer's assurance cannot remove that condition. The officer should avoid signing a certificate that misstates the integrity assessment or the printing procedure. The actual performed steps and detected facts govern what can truthfully be certified.

sections.heading: Read the recording provision with its conditions
sections.body: Section 18-220(c) provides a clerk-of-circuit-court acceptance rule for a qualifying tangible copy containing a sufficient certificate and the executing officer's accurate-copy certification. It excludes plats recorded under the cited real-property title. Subsection(d) also identifies conditions for the certificate's prima-facie evidentiary effect. The provision should be applied to its stated record and certificate facts instead of assumed to cover every electronic printout unconditionally.

faqs.q: Must the officer supervise or perform printing?
faqs.a: Section 18-204(e)(1)(ii) expressly requires personally printing or supervising it.

faqs.q: Can a detected electronic-signature error be ignored?
faqs.a: The statute prohibits the certification when the stated change or error is detected.

articles.keyword: Maryland remote tangible declaration three days
articles.intent: Follow the Maryland tangible declaration sequence
articles.title: Maryland's Three-Day Tangible Declaration Method
articles.description: Track recorded signing, secure declaration, transmission and certificate execution.
articles.h1: Following a Maryland Remote Tangible Record
articles.lede: Section 18-214 supplies a defined declaration method for a tangible record outside the notary's physical presence. Its sequence preserves the connection between the live act and the received papers.

sections.heading: Record both signatures under the method
sections.body: Under subsection(c), the principal signs the tangible record and a declaration during the audiovisual recording. The declaration is part of or securely attached to the record and carries the statutory same-record assurance in substantially the provided form. A notary should plan the record-declaration package before the session so the recording captures both required signing events and the papers remain connected afterward.

sections.heading: Send the complete package within three days
sections.body: The principal sends the tangible record and declaration no later than three days after the notarial act. The deadline belongs to Maryland's specified method and is not established by a courier's preferred schedule. Sending only the final signature page would leave the stated record-and-declaration procedure incomplete. Completeness and timing both support the notary's reasonable confirmation that the received instrument is the record involved in the live session.

sections.heading: Execute the certificate after receipt
sections.body: After receiving the tangible record and declaration, the notary executes the required certificate with the prescribed or similar statement about witnessing the individual sign by communication technology. Subsection(e) makes a compliant act effective on the declaration-signing date. This is a specific statutory sequence. The later receipt of papers should not be used to invent unrelated certificate facts or omit the required remote-method statement.

sections.heading: Keep the other remote duties in place
sections.body: Subsection(f) preserves other procedures satisfying the same-record requirement. Whichever lawful method is used, the notary remains physically in Maryland, establishes identity, records the performance and keeps the required records. The certificate indicates the remote individual and communication technology. An alternative document method does not eliminate the journal, ten-year recording retention or the applicable notification and authorization process.

faqs.q: When are both papers transmitted under this method?
faqs.a: No later than three days after the act.

faqs.q: Does subsection(c) prohibit all other record-confirmation procedures?
faqs.a: Subsection(f) preserves another procedure satisfying the statutory same-record requirement.

articles.keyword: Maryland remote notary all persons physical location
articles.title: The Maryland Remote Session Includes the Room
articles.description: Apply the entire-location and participant-role requirements alongside identity and recording duties.
articles.h1: Recording the Remote Location and Participants
articles.lede: A clear view of the principal's face is only part of Maryland's remote procedure. COMAR also addresses the physical setting and the other people present.

sections.heading: Use technology that captures the required setting
sections.body: COMAR 01.02.08.07 A(4) requires technology capable of making an audiovisual record of the entire physical location of the act and all physically present persons. Imagine a principal framed tightly on camera while companions remain outside view. The notary should establish the required technology-supported location record. A pen closeup or silent still image does not provide the broader audiovisual setting described by the regulation.

sections.heading: Identify each person's role
sections.body: SubsectionA(5) requires all persons physically with the remote individual to identify themselves and their role in the transaction. The rule is not limited to employees or people who will sign the instrument. Understanding who is present supports an accurate account of the session and the notary's own judgment about the principal's participation. A companion should not remain an unidentified off-camera participant merely because the principal has already shown identification.

sections.heading: Apply identity and voluntary-execution rules separately
sections.body: The remote identity statute permits personal knowledge, a qualifying credible witness or the documentary combination of presentation, analysis and proofing. Those methods identify the principal. Section 18-207 separately permits refusal when the officer is unsatisfied of capacity or knowing voluntary signing, subject to other law. An identified principal can still be pressured by a companion. Recording the setting does not remove the officer's responsibility for the actual lawful ceremony.

sections.heading: Retain the performance and state the method
sections.body: The notary creates and retains the audiovisual record for at least ten years under COMAR.07. The journal separately records the act, identity evidence, fee and remote appearance mode. The certificate states that a remotely located individual and communication technology were involved. These records preserve different aspects of the appointment. A successful video connection does not by itself establish completion of every required identity, record and certificate step.

faqs.q: Who identifies themselves during the remote appointment?
faqs.a: All persons physically present with the remote individual identify themselves and their roles.

faqs.q: Does the audiovisual recording replace the journal?
faqs.a: The journal remains a separate statutory record of the act.

articles.keyword: Maryland notary journal repository successor retention
articles.title: Maryland Records after Resignation or Death
articles.description: Review last-act retention, approved storage and separate recording-successor notice.
articles.lede: The journal and remote recordings can outlast the officer's commission. Their succession and retention provisions should be planned as distinct obligations.

sections.heading: Use the last act in the journal
sections.body: Section 18-219(a) requires ten years of journal retention after the last act chronicled. A book opened many years ago but used recently remains subject to that later anchor. Retirement, an office move or purchase of a replacement volume does not change it. The journal must preserve the required contemporaneous entries in its compliant tangible or electronic format rather than being replaced by a monthly revenue summary.

sections.heading: Report location after specified cessation
sections.body: On resignation, revocation or suspension, subsection(e) requires retention and notice to the Secretary of the journal's location, subject to the approved alternatives. A current or former notary can transmit it to a repository approved by the Secretary or store it through another manner approved in regulations. The statute does not make any cheap storage company automatically qualified. The actual approval supporting the alternative should be established.

sections.heading: Identify the responsible successor
sections.body: After death or adjudicated incompetency, the personal representative, guardian or another knowing possessor follows the journal disposition provisions in subsection(g). The person holding the volume should not treat it as ordinary disposable office stationery. The official record continues to serve the acts it chronicles. The statutory recipient or approved storage route preserves continuity when the original officer can no longer maintain the journal personally.

sections.heading: Handle remote recordings under their own provision
sections.body: Section 18-214(j) separately addresses recording retention and a guardian, conservator, agent or personal representative who assumes authority over those recordings. That successor notifies the Secretary within thirty days and follows maintenance/storage requirements. The recording period is at least ten years under the statute and COMAR. A journal transfer does not silently satisfy the distinct successor notice for remote recordings, and storage should preserve the actual audiovisual performance record.

faqs.q: Does the journal's purchase date control retention?
faqs.a: The statute uses ten years after the last act chronicled.

faqs.q: What notice applies when a successor assumes remote-recording authority?
faqs.a: Section 18-214(j)(2) requires notice to the Secretary within thirty days.
